purpose: Re-run the first Branch FLINTLOCK-equivalent suppression cycle with the previously omitted Gilbert land-air/search system and corrected Japanese water-air/Eniwetok composition.
rollback_boundary: Only the 2-Feb 04:30 onward local-air calculation is replaced. Jan31 carrier visual, Jan31-night submarine recontact, 8-aircraft Japanese night strike, 1-Feb second-TG recognition and the Japanese fleet-carrier holding posture remain realized working events.

US_TF58_first_cycle.role: decisive fighter sweep + radar/radio/runway + dispersed-aircraft suppression; large CAP/ASW/search reserve retained because Japanese fleet carriers remain unlocated.

US_Gilbert_land_air_parallel.effect: Adds staggered B-24/B-25 pressure to northern/central bases, stronger Mili/Jaluit suppression and persistent search/ASW. It does not become a second 365-aircraft carrier wave.

Japanese_warning_and_launch.usable_warning: 18-26 min at best surviving Taroa/Roi nodes; outer nodes vary. Pre-existing alert and water/shore search prevent complete surprise.
Japanese_warning_and_launch.Kyofu_local_intercepts: 4-6 aircraft may contest low/medium attacks over Mili/Jaluit/Wotje water/shore zones; subset of fighter total and not mixed into high-altitude main CAP.
Japanese_warning_and_launch.water_recon_effect: Float/Zuiun detachments preserve contact/confirmation capacity and some warning after runway damage, but cannot replace radar/plot or sustain fighter sweeps.

losses_2Feb_morning_only.guard: US loss total includes carrier and Gilbert land-air aircraft only for the 2-Feb morning. It does not include the earlier Japanese night raid, which caused no US aircraft/ship loss.

cumulative_from_31Jan_night_through_2Feb.note: Includes the 4 G4M-class losses in the Jan31/1Feb night strike plus the 2-Feb morning losses; do not subtract twice.

base_effects.state: Main radar/plot/runway hit hard; dispersed aircraft and some water/recon support survive.
base_effects.runway: intermittent/emergency strips with repair parties active

base_effects.state: Primary communications/radar and runway heavily suppressed; fighter direction degraded.
base_effects.C2: B centered, locally lower during outages

base_effects.state: Seaplane ramp/fuel/anchorage/support points deliberately attacked in addition to runway-area targets. 952/Zuiun layer takes losses but is not erased.
base_effects.water_ops: 5-7 serviceable float/fast-recon aircraft centered remain in the Ebeye/Kwaj system immediately after first cycle.

base_effects.state: Carrier attack field and water/recon support receive combined carrier + land-air pressure.
Gilbert A-24/P-39/P-40/B-25 pressure materially stronger than v039 modeled; local fighter/Kyofu layer remains but sortie generation falls.
Runway plus seaplane/anchorage infrastructure pressured separately; water layer survives in reduced form.
Not a primary first-morning target in the corrected centerline; most of the 11-land-attack serviceable reservoir survives for later-day/night threat.

post_cycle_marshall_air_state.search_capacity: 4-6 useful long-range/search-confirmation sorties per day remain plausible through surviving water/recon aircraft and alternate communications; one extra fast confirmation sortie may be surged on a high-value cue. This is more resilient than runway-only accounting but less than Jan28 6-8 + 1-2 surge.

reverse_bearing_contact.event: A surviving fast Japanese reconnaissance aircraft uses the returning strike stream/recovery axis and obtains a short visual on one US TG: three carrier decks strongly identified with three fast battleships/heavy screen, about 120-160 nmi from the Kwajalein battle area.
reverse_bearing_contact.carrier_gate: First-line Japanese carrier GO remains WITHHELD; contact is valuable enough for submarine convergence and eastward conditional closure, but other US TG geometry and recovery/egress remain insufficient.

US_operational_assessment: The corrected network makes the US operation more systemically powerful than v039 because Gilbert land-air suppresses outer bases and maintains reconnaissance/ASW. It does not make first-cycle losses vanish: warned Taroa/Roi defenders and Raiden still inflict meaningful cost.
Japan_operational_assessment: Local air strength is somewhat lower after the corrected morning than v039, but the water-air and Eniwetok depth means the Marshall system is still not decapitated. Surviving search/night-strike capability remains enough to matter if submarine/air contact freshness is maintained.
next_exact_action: Run 2-Feb late morning/afternoon with the corrected poststate: TF58 second suppression cycle, Gilbert land-air outer-base pressure, and submarine convergence against the fresh three-carrier TG. Resolve whether a CV/CVL/AO/escort weapon-quality opportunity occurs before the remaining Marshall network is further suppressed.
